verdict_reason: The new commodity-page bullets match the code (announcement rules, focus, Update selected, named headings via commodityNameFor, sort by code, Latin-name chips, fetch fallback); only three Minor wording/design items remain.

todos.issue: Line 266 says the shared results mean 'every rule below holds on both paths', but the bullets below include rules that hold on one path only: the 'Update selected' button (no-JS only, hidden with JS, line 271-274), Escape/click-away hiding the list (JS only, line 287-290) and the fetch-failure fallback (JS only, line 294-295). The sentence is untrue as written.
todos.fix: Must: the bullet claims parity only for what both paths share (the results markup and the selection rules), not for every following bullet. One way: 'The results are the ones the page renders without JavaScript, so the ordering, labelling and selection rules below hold on both paths.'

todos.issue: Line 293 says Clear all sits beside the count 'as a link', but _results.njk renders it as <button type="submit" class="govuk-link app-link-button" name="action" value="clear">, a form POST styled as a link. The same doc describes 'Create a new notification' as 'a form button styled as a link' (line 125) and states elsewhere that removals are POSTs so a link cannot trigger them; 'as a link' invites a reader to think Clear all is a GET.
todos.fix: Must: the doc says Clear all is a form button styled as a link that posts the page form. One way: 'Clear all sits beside the count, as a form button styled as a link.'

todos.issue: The design source announces the count without singular handling: GB-notification-service app/assets/javascripts/commodity-search.js:649 (commit fe772a8) does announce(`${speciesRowCount} results available`), so one match reads '1 results available'. The code pluralises instead: copy.en.js:15 resultsAvailable: (count) => `${plural(count, 'result')} available`, giving '1 result available'. The GOV.UK style guide (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/style-guide/a-to-z-of-gov-uk-style) expects grammatical plain English, and the GOV.UK accessible-autocomplete announces '1 result is available'. page-design.md:296-297 parks this as 'open with the designer' rather than raising it.
todos.fix: Must: the designer rules on the singular announcement, and page-design.md states the ruled behaviour with no open-question note. Question for the designer: for one matching species, keep '1 result available' (grammatical, as built), or announce '1 results available' as the prototype does?
